title: The `final` keyword on variables, methods and classes

videos.script: One word, final, in three places, and it means something slightly different in each. {{variables}} On a variable, it means assigned once. On a field, once per object, and the compiler checks that every constructor does it. A book's ISBN is the obvious candidate. {{references}} But final on a reference fixes the arrow, not the thing it points at. A final string builder can still be appended to. That catches almost everyone once. {{classes}} On a method, final means no subclass may replace it. On a class, it means no subclass at all. String is final, and the reason is that everything else trusts it. {{capture}} Last, a rule you will meet before you know its name. Code inside another piece of code may read a local variable only if that variable never changes. The compiler calls it effectively final. By the end you know what each final protects, and what it does not.
